text: Why is the return type not part of a method's signature?
choices: A call that discards the result would be ambiguous
Because Java only allows one return type
It is part of the signature
Because the JVM erases return types
explanation: Given int g(int) and long g(int), the call g(5); with the result discarded gives the compiler nothing to choose from. Rather than allow it sometimes, Java forbids it always.
